DERETH TOWN TOUR - SOUNDTRACK LICENSE RECORD
============================================

File:      /mnt/wbterminal2/film-projects/dereth-town-tour/song/music.mp3
Format:    MP3, 320 kbps CBR, 44.1 kHz, stereo (made from the original 48 kHz / 24-bit FLAC files)
Duration:  3431.86 s  (57:11.86), measured with ffprobe on the final file
Assembled: 2026-10-14

WORK
----
Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827)
  1. Egmont Overture, Op. 84 (1810)                     - concert-opening overture
  2. Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, Op. 55 "Eroica" (1803-04), four movements

Both are purely instrumental. There are no sung lyrics.

PERFORMER
---------
Czech National Symphony Orchestra, credited as "Musopen Symphony". Recorded in Prague
for the Musopen Kickstarter Project in 2012.

LICENSES
--------
Composition:  PUBLIC DOMAIN worldwide. The composer died in 1827. The Commons template is
              {{PD-old-auto-expired|deathyear=1827}}.
Recording:    PUBLIC DOMAIN. Musopen paid for these recordings through its 2010 Kickstarter
              campaign and released them to the public domain. The Commons template is
              {{PD-author|Musopen}}, and the Internet Archive marks the files with the
              Public Domain Mark 1.0 (http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/).
No attribution is legally required. The credit line below is given as a courtesy.

EDITS
-----
- 1.0 s of silence was added after the Egmont Overture, so the gap before the symphony is 1.7 s.
- The tail of Eroica I was trimmed by 0.07 s, with a 0.4 s fade over room tone.
- The tail of Eroica II was trimmed from 3.37 s of silence to 1.0 s, with a 0.6 s fade over room tone.
- The tail of Eroica IV was trimmed from 2.67 s of silence to 1.0 s, with a 0.8 s fade over room tone.
- No leading silence was longer than 1 s, so the starts were not trimmed.
- The audio was resampled from 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz with soxr at precision 28 and encoded with
  libmp3lame at 320k. The level was not normalised. The peak is -0.8 dBFS and the mean is
  -22.7 dB, so the orchestra's dynamics are kept.

CREDIT LINE
-----------
Music: Ludwig van Beethoven - Egmont Overture, Op. 84 and Symphony No. 3 "Eroica", Op. 55.
Performed by the Czech National Symphony Orchestra (Musopen Symphony), courtesy of Musopen (musopen.org).
Public domain.

WHY THIS RECORDING
------------------
- The Musopen Kickstarter set has the best documented public-domain release of any complete
  orchestral recording found. Its files are lossless 24-bit and it is a professional orchestra.
- The Eroica alone runs 48.2 min, which is under the 50-70 min target. The Egmont Overture is
  from the same sessions, orchestra and composer, so it was added as a concert-style opener,
  bringing the total to 57.2 min.
- These candidates were rejected:
  - Bruckner 7 by the Munich HSO: the recording is CC BY-SA 4.0.
  - Mahler 5 by the Peabody SO: 70.9 min, and it was uploaded to archive.org by a third party,
    so its provenance is unclear.
  - Mahler 7 by Utah/Abravanel and Scheherazade by Monteux 1942: both are labelled "CC0", but they
    are commercial label recordings, so the claim is doubtful.
  - Omega13a MuseScore renders: CC BY.
  - The Goldberg Variations by Shelley Katz (Musopen, public domain): 76 min, which is too long.

No single orchestral work in Category:Musopen_Kickstarter_Project runs 50-70 min. The longest are Eroica at
48.2 min, Tchaikovsky 6 at 46.0 and Brahms 1 at 45.6. The only longer item is the Goldberg Variations, which is
solo piano and runs 76.1 min. So Egmont followed by the Eroica stays the choice.
The final file is MP3, 320 kbps, 44,100 Hz, stereo, 3431.86 s long. The longest silence in it is 1.72 s, and the 5 ID3 chapters are present.
